svg.title: Starlight bent by the Sun
svg.desc: Light from a distant star passes close to the Sun and is bent toward it on its way to an observer on the Earth. Tracing the arriving ray straight back, the observer sees the star at an apparent position farther from the Sun than its actual position. The distances are not to scale. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Starlight passing closer to the Sun is deflected more
Weak-field general relativity gives about 1.75 arcsec at the solar limb. The broken ray is schematic
with exaggerated bending; it is not a numerical geodesic or a drawing to scale.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
